A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STUN and contain readable methods, equations, results, figures, and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning experiments on Arctic, Mixtral, and Llama-2, including benchmark results and clustering/reconstruction ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and reports additional comparator results, approximation comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and cost measurements.

M1.justification: The clustering, representative selection, selective reconstruction, and subsequent OWL/Wanda pruning procedures remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 move from the appendix into the main text; the additional probability definition supports the derivation without changing the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain C4 calibration data, GSM8K, and the same eight NLU benchmarks. OLMoE-7B adds a model configuration, without a documented new dataset or task. Evaluation under skewed data distributions is proposed only as future work.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with LLM-Pruner in Figure 1 and Table 2, and SEER-MoE, Expert Drop, and Layer Drop in Table 4. These substantially expand the structured and efficient pruning alternatives beyond v1's comparisons with OWL, Wanda, and Lu et al.

E3.justification: v2 adds a fixed-50%-sparsity interpolation comparison, OLMoE-7B evaluations, and higher-sparsity points for Arctic and Mixtral-8x22B. Table 4 explicitly uses different metrics following He et al., although their specification is limited. Existing calibration, quantization, and hyperparameter search grids are retained.

E4.justification: The original clustering and reconstruction ablations survive as Tables 8–10. v2 adds an O(n)-versus-O(1) comparison, reports sensitivity to similarity weights and expert sparsity, provides expert-only results, and introduces a dedicated cost analysis. These substantially broaden evidence about approximation quality, tuning, and efficiency.

E5.justification: Both implementation appendices state that evaluation is performed once because no randomness is introduced. v2 adds no repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original main-table and clustering/reconstruction ablation scores are retained. New results include Table 5's GSM8K scores of 53.22 for STUN's expert pruning versus 48.52 for Lu et al. at 25% sparsity, additional comparator and OLMoE results, and cost and kurtosis measurements. Some low-sparsity Arctic points from v1 Figure 1 are no longer reported.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix A.1, Equation 10, explicitly defines joint pruning probability through normalized inverse reconstruction loss, supporting an equivalence previously asserted without that definition. Most derivations are relocated unchanged. v1 Section 5's targeted-dropout formulation and its connection to MoE training are removed.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly makes outperforming both structured-only and unstructured-only pruning a headline contribution, whereas v1 primarily emphasizes outperforming unstructured-only pruning. The central O(1) scalability and Arctic performance-at-40%-sparsity claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 removes the targeted-dropout explanation for inherent robustness to expert pruning while retaining the kurtosis-based argument for subsequent unstructured pruning. Appendix F adds a generation-versus-multiple-choice explanation for GSM8K difficulty. The limitations newly identify highly imbalanced or skewed data distributions as unevaluated.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised code release with stated public availability and an access link. It adds CPU-time information and method-specific GPU pruning times in Table 7. Existing C4 sample counts, sequence lengths, quantization, hardware, and reconstruction settings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds efficient expert-pruning references, including Liu, Zhang, Muzio, and He, and GPU sparsity references such as Mishra and Zhao. It removes the targeted-dropout and regularization discussion and associated citations. The broader positioning as combined structured and unstructured pruning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around inter- and intra-expert sparsity. Detailed derivations move into Appendix A, algorithms move into the main text, the original ablation discussion moves into Appendix D, and a dedicated Cost Analysis section is introduced.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the introductory plot, adds a method schematic and comparison taxonomy, and expands the MoE figure from three to four panels with revised axis ranges. It condenses the main expert-comparison table while retaining its detailed counterpart in the appendix, and adds multiple comparison and analysis tables.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central design: additional structured and efficient pruning comparisons address v1's limited comparator coverage, while the O(n)-versus-O(1), sensitivity, and cost analyses directly support approximation and scalability choices. Reorganization and code-access information improve usability. New reporting weaknesses temper these gains: Table 4's unpruned average is 71.5 despite the displayed scores averaging about 73.6, and OLMoE evaluation details are sparse. These localized issues do not outweigh the stronger overall support for the contributions.
